To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
siblings are more likely to migrate to the same internal/external destination as preceding siblings.
the probability of remittances and the amount of remittance sent are not significantly affected by the presence of other remitting siblings.
The presence of other sibling migrants has a statistically significant negative effect on the migration decisions of other siblings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the migration and remittance behaviour of Kenyan siblings and the impact of remittances on the expenditure patterns and the use of remittances.
the factors that influence subsequent migration and remittance decisions of Kenyan households.
the determinants of international migration and remittancing decisions in Kenya, and the impact of remittances on the expenditure patterns and uses of remittancing households.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the findings of this thesis are consistent with the theoretical framework that migration is a joint household level and remittance behaviour a group level decision.
the migration and remittance behaviour of Kenyan siblings is not only influenced by the migration behaviour of other siblings but also by other household level factors.
remittances play an important role in the economic well-being of migrant households.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
migration and remittancing are important factors that influence expenditure patterns of households in developing countries such as Kenya.

remittance sending decisions are made independently of the decisions to migrate, and that remittances do not appear to be pooled with general income when households allocate their budgets towards physical investments and durable good categories.
the findings obtained in this thesis have important implications for policy makers in Kenya.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the decision to migrate is a household decision and that the presence of other migrants has a negative effect on the migration decision of other household members.
the migration and remittance behaviour of Kenyan households is influenced by the presence of other migrants in the network.
remittances have an impact on household expenditure and the decision of whether to remit depends on the number of migrants in the household.
